exercise.name: Wide-Grip EZ Bar Curl
library_steps: Hold the EZ bar on the outer bends, palms up, arms straight.
Keep your elbows at your sides and curl the bar to your chest.
Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing, an EZ bar held palms up on the outer bends; elbows by the sides bend from ~8 to ~125 deg. Biceps does the work, brachioradialis helps.

setup.target: EZ bar, hands on the outer (wide) bends, palms up and turned in a little by the camber.
setup.why: Library step 1; MARC tested the EZ-bar curl.

muscles.emg: Main elbow flexor in curls; above 50 % of max RMS in standing and preacher curls.
The EZ bar raised brachioradialis EMG over the dumbbell curl (MARC); higher than biceps when lowering (UYS).
muscles.role: Helps bend the elbow, most with the palm turned down.
muscles.surface: Thumb side of the upper forearm.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Upper arms swing up with the bar.

sources.citation: Marcolin G, Panizzolo FA, Petrone N, et al. 2018. Differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl. PeerJ 6:e5165.
sources.what_it_gave: Dumbbell, straight-bar and EZ-bar curls at 65 % 1RM: the EZ bar gave higher biceps and brachioradialis EMG than the dumbbell curl; straight vs EZ bar differed little.

sources.citation: Oliveira LF, Matta TT, Alves DS, Garcia MA, Vieira TM. 2009. Effect of the shoulder position on the biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls. J Sports Sci Med 8(1):24-29.
sources.what_it_gave: Standing, incline and preacher curls: biceps long head above 50 % of max RMS in all; with the upper arm fixed in front (preacher) the biceps worked hardest only over a short early range.

sources.citation: Uysal A, Karaduman B, Soslu R, et al. 2026. Effects of grip variation on biceps brachii and brachioradialis electromyographic activity during concentric and eccentric phases of the barbell curl exercise. BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil.
sources.what_it_gave: Barbell curls with supinated, semi-supinated and neutral grip bars: biceps and brachioradialis both highly active; brachioradialis above biceps in the lowering phase.
